### Construction and Working of N-Channel Enhancement MOSFET (E-MOSFET)

#### Construction
- It consists of a lightly doped p-type substrate into which two heavily doped n+ regions (source and drain) are diffused.
- Unlike the depletion MOSFET, **there is no physical channel** between the source and drain; the p-substrate extends all the way to the $\text{SiO}_2$ insulating layer under the gate.
- A metal gate is placed on top of the silicon dioxide layer.

#### Working Operation
1. **When $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$**: With $V_{DS}$ applied and $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$, the two back-to-back p-n junctions prevent current flow. Thus, $I_D = 0$.
2. **When $V_{GS} > V_{Th}$ (Threshold Voltage)**: When a positive voltage greater than the threshold voltage ($V_{Th}$) is applied to the gate, it repels holes away from the region beneath the gate and attracts minority carrier electrons from the p-substrate toward the $\text{SiO}_2$ layer.
3. **Inversion Layer**: These accumulated electrons form an induced **n-channel** connecting the source and drain, allowing drain current ($I_D$) to flow when $V_{DS}$ is applied.

### Characteristics
- **Drain Characteristics**: Shows curves of $I_D$ vs $V_{DS}$ for different values of $V_{GS}$. Regions include ohmic/triode and saturation.
- **Transfer Characteristics**: A square-law plot of $I_D$ vs $V_{GS}$, starting only after $V_{GS} = V_{Th}$.
proTip: Note that enhancement MOSFETs only operate in enhancement mode (hence $V_{GS}$ must be positive for N-channel).
